_why:
The spec declares `responsible.type` of the KYC document as an ARRAY. The real Asaas returns a STRING.

Proven against the real sandbox:
  GET /v3/myAccount/documents
  → { "data": [ { "responsible": { "name": "Pr Soluções Sandbox", "type": "INDIVIDUAL_COMPANY" } } ] }

And the spec contradicts itself, which confirms which side is wrong: the field is declared `"type": "array"`, but its `example` is the SCALAR `"ASSOCIATION"`, and the `enum` hangs on the array instead of on the `items`. It is the signature of Asaas's spec generator bug — the same one progress.md already catalogs in six other DTOs.

Without this overlay the damage is subtle and expensive: we return the RIGHT string, and our own contract validation — generated from the spec — rejected the response. The simulator was forced to choose between being right and passing its own contract.
